Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.
1. Heard Sri Vijay Prakash Chaturvedi, learned counsel for the appellants and learned A.G.A. for the State.
None has turned up for respondent no.2, despite personal service of notice.

2. By means of this criminal appeal, the appellants have challenged the cognizance/summoning order dated 19.9.2022 passed by Special Session Judge, SC/ST (P.A.) Act, Siddharth Nagar in Special Criminal Case No.471 of 2022 (State vs. Saurabh Viswash), arising out of Case Crime No.101 of 2022, under Section 504 I.P.C. and 3(1)Dha SC/ST (P.A.) Act, Police Station Chilhiya, District Siddharth Nagar, by which the present appellants Manoj Kumar and Shikha have been summoned to face trial for the offences under Section 504 I.P.C. and Section 3(1)Dha of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

sentences.text: 3. It is vehemently contended on behalf of appellants that impugned cognizance/summoning order is bad in law, inasmuch it has been passed ignoring the fact that there has not been prima facie any evidence against them which could constitute any offence under Section 504 I.P.C. and Section 3(1)Dha of SC/ST Act.
It is contended that the order is per se illegal.

It is further contended that the name of the appellants has been introduced just to harass them and to take advantage of the scheme Manoj Kumar And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87466804/
1 run by the government for grant of compensation as well as to extort money from the innocent persons by bulldozing them into legal machinery so that they go through unnecessary hassles of facing trial.

sentences.text: There has not been any substance in the allegations and that there is no evidence to support them.

4. My attention has been drawn to another FIR (Case Crime No.298 of 2021) lodged by the victim of the case against three persons named therein alleging that between 7.3.2021 to 25.5.2021 one of the persons named in that FIR, in pursuance of a conspiracy hatched by his parents (who too have been named in the FIR) took her to different places and committed rape on her on a false assurance of marriage and that despite her attempts no FIR was registered against those persons, therefore, she has been compelled to move an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
It may be noted that on the basis of that application moved by the so called victim a Case Crime No.298 of 2021, under Sections 376, 506, 120-B I.P.C. was registered.
It may be noted that in the instant case similar allegations have been imputed against Saurabh Viswash and his parents by father of the victim.

My attention has further been drawn to an order passed by this Court on an application moved under Section 482 Cr.P.C. with regard to cognizance/summoning order arising out of Case Crime No.298 of 2021 as aforesaid, whereby further proceedings of the criminal case were ordered to be stayed.
It is contended on behalf of appellants that the so called victim is habitual of filing false cases for ulterior motives.
5. I went through the material on record.
As per the allegations in the FIR, the daughter of the informant became friendly with one Dr. Saurabh Viswash and developed physical relation with him.
It is stated therein that the parents of Saurabh Viswash agreed to arrange marriage of his son with the daughter of the informant.
Later on, they dragged their feet off.
6. In the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the so called victim has narrated the same story.

If all the statements given by the victim and his father (the informant) are taken into consideration, it becomes quite clear that the victim had developed physical sexual relation with accused Saurabh Viswash in a consensual manner.
The only allegations against the present appellants are that they declined to marry of their son with the victim.
There is not a single allegation which can bring the case within the definition of Section 3(1)Dha of SC/ST Act.
There is no evidence disclosing that the appellants ever abused or used foul language taking caste name in public or did any act so as to bring the act within the definition of Section 504 I.P.C.
It may also be usefully noticed that there is admittedly no allegation under Section 376 I.P.C. against the instant appellants.
7. I went through the impugned order.
It appears that the learned trial court has in quite a mechanical way passed an order summoning the present appellants.

It can be very well inferred from the summoning order that the learned trial court has not made any effort to go through the evidence on record and the prosecution papers and has passed the order in a very cursory and cavalier manner.
8. Therefore, I am of the view that the impugned cognizance/summoning order as far as the present appellants are concerned is illegal, arbitrary and passed against the evidence on record.
